sentences.text:
Order 
This miscellaneous appeal has been preferred by the appellant/claimant for enhancement of the amount of award by Rs.3,05,600/- against the award dated 20.02.2009 passed by the Second Additional MACT, Morena, in Claim Case No.111/2007 whereby learned MACT has awarded an amount of Rs.2,14,400/- along with interest @ 7% per annum to the claimant for the injuries suffered in road accident.
2. The necessary facts for disposal of this appeal are that the appellant was the driver of the offending vehicle on monthly salary of Rs.3,000/- per month.

On 13.06.2007 the appellant was driving the said vehicle and at about 11.00 pm the said truck collided with the culvert of Goraghat in between Gwalior and Shivpuri and after breaking culvert it capsized.

In the said accident,
D.P.Verma and Laxminarayan, who were sitting in the vehicle, sustained injuries and two other persons died.
The appellant sustained NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14194 2 MA-762-2009 grievous injuries in the accident.

3. Learned counsel for the L.Rs. of appellant submits that learned Tribunal has erroneously assumed 50% permanent disability to the claimant while it ought to be 100% in the light of the statement of Dr. Arvind Kumar (AW- 2).

It is also submitted that Dr. Arvind Kumar has categorically submitted in his statement that vision of both the eyes of the claimant has reduced to the extent that he was only able to recognize light and movement of hand, and therefore, he sustained 100% permanent disablement in eyes.

It is also submitted that income of the appellant has also been assumed on lower side as Rs.1,800/- per month, while on the date of accident the minimum wages of a skilled labourer were Rs.2,820/-, and therefore, the minimum wages of a skilled labourer ought to be considered as the income of Rampal Singh vs Jeevesh Sharma on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39324410/
1 injured/claimant.
Hence, on two counts, learned counsel prays for enhancement of the amount of compensation.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company has submitted that learned Tribunal has erroneously assumed permanent disability even as 50%.
There is no scientific ground behind such assumption.
It is also submitted that learned Tribunal on the basis of material available on record has assessed the amount of compensation.
It is further submitted that permanent disability certificate has not been filed showing the percentage of permanent disability and no witness has been examined in that respect to prove it.
Ex.P/53 does not reveal any percentage of permanent disability.

It is also submitted that claim petition has been filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, and therefore, no other ground for NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:14194 3 MA-762-2009 enhancement is there.
The claimants are entitled to get the compensation strictly according to the schedule.
There is no ground for enhancement.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
5. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.
6 . Dr. Arvind Kumar Dubey (AW-2) has stated in his statement that on 11.08.2007 he has examined the claimant Rampal Singh.
At that time, his vision in right eye was only limited to perception of light and hand movements.
His left eye was found to have corneal scarring with neuropathy.
He further stated in his statement that opinion for operation has been given.
After operation the patient could only recognize finger from a distance of 3 meters.
Since there was scar on macula, therefore, no further treatment could have been possible.
He became unable for any employment.
He has given the permanent disability certificate (Ex.P/53).

Though in cross-examination he has stated that the claimant is not able to work as driver and because of occupational blindness, permanent disability shall be deemed to be 100%, but it is also stated by him that he can do other business with the help of attender.
7 . Admittedly, there is no permanent disability certificate.

Ex.P/53 is an information given by Dr.
Arvind Kumar Dubey (AW-2).

Admittedly, no certificate of permanent disability has been sought from the Medical Board of the concerned area where the claimant resides and no reason for not obtaining such certificate has been shown by the claimant in his statement.
Dr. Arvind Kumar Dubey (AW-2) is not a treating doctor.
He has examined the claimant on 11.08.2007 and issued Ex.P/53.
This letter (Ex.P/53) does NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14194 4 MA-762-2009 not contain the percentage of permanent disability.
This document contains date 04.03.2008.

If Dr. Arvind Kumar Dubey (AW-2) has examined the claimant on 11.08.2007, then he has to issue the said certificate on that date or within 2-3 days, but Ex.P/53 has been issued after a period of almost seven months.
It is no where stated by this witness that on 04.03.2008 or just before issuing Ex.P/53 he has again examined the claimant.
In these circumstances, keeping in view the material on record, learned Tribunal has rightly found only 50% permanent disability to the claimant.
Conclusion in this regard of the learned Tribunal cannot be said to be perverse or illegal.

8. So far as the contention of learned counsel for the appellant in respect of income of the appellant/claimant assumed by the learned Tribunal on lower side is concerned, the learned Tribunal has assumed the income of the appellant as driver @ Rs.1,800/- per month, but on the Rampal Singh vs Jeevesh Sharma on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39324410/
2 date of accident the minimum wages of a skilled labourer were Rs.2,820/- per month.

Therefore,
instead of Rs.1,800/- per month, the income of the appellant as driver ought to be assumed as Rs.2,820/- per month.
9. The claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, therefore, the claimant is not entitled to compensation on other heads like future prospect etc.

10. Consequently, the appeal is allowed in above terms and the appellant would be entitled for the following compensation:-

Yearly income 21,600/- 33,840/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14194 5 MA-762-2009 Loss of income 33,840x18 =6,09,120/-

on account of 1,94,400/-
x 50%=3,04,560/-
50% PD Pain & suffering 5.
Medical 6.
Enhanced compensation shall carry interest @ 6% per annum.
Rest of the terms & conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE ms/-
